{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-ne-o","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"f3a7d29409130fcc636a90c76c275c538a5dc13dd6e5bbd35106ca719d06752d","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-ne-class-o:lineage:40","source_registry_sha256":"66161d94cc863d3cf353417f54f101bf8681de71fc4c3b73f43c86f2be1c7398","source_liveness_sha256":"78587b1f8f8617c7b8b0a43b3f0679698b900b7d64ddfc387c1773ac070571e8"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Traffic-sign meanings and work-zone devices","heading":"Traffic-sign meanings and work-zone devices","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Traffic-sign meanings and work-zone devices

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A47
An Added Lane sign means entering traffic has its own new lane, so no merge is needed at that point. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A47
An Advisory Exit Speed sign gives the recommended safe speed for leaving a freeway or expressway. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A47
At a Slippery When Wet warning, reduce speed and use caution because wet pavement may be slick. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A47
A Lane Ends warning means the lane will terminate and a merge will be needed. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A47
Do not pass beneath a low-clearance structure if the vehicle is taller than the posted clearance. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A47
A Hill warning indicates a steep downgrade and advises checking the brakes. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A47
A Deer Crossing warning calls for alertness and slowing if a deer is seen. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A47
Deer warnings mark higher-conflict locations, but deer may cross on any Nebraska roadway. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A47
A Horse-Drawn Vehicle sign warns that slow horse-drawn vehicles commonly cross or share the road there. [A47]
Source: [A47 -> pdf-0047]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A48
At a Pedestrian Crossing warning, slow down, yield to people crossing and stop if needed. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A48
A School Advance Crossing sign warns of an upcoming schoolchildren's crosswalk. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A48
A School Crossing sign is placed where children cross; obey the crossing guard's signs. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R13 | anchor: A48
A Bicycle warning calls for watching for people cycling across the road. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R14 | anchor: A48
A Reverse Turn sign warns of a sharp turn followed by a turn the other way; the first direction varies with the sign. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R15 | anchor: A48
A Reverse Curve sign warns of a curve followed by one in the opposite direction; left-first and right-first versions exist. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R16 | anchor: A48
A Curve warning identifies a gradual bend and calls for slowing to the indicated safe speed. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R17 | anchor: A48
An advisory-speed plaque adds a recommended speed for the condition described by a diamond warning sign. [A48]
Source: [A48 -> pdf-0048]

FACT_ID: sec08-R18 | anchor: A49
A Winding Road warning means several turns or curves lie ahead. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R19 | anchor: A49
A Crossroad warning identifies a four-way intersection and calls for watching cross traffic. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R20 | anchor: A49
At a T-intersection warning, the road ends ahead and a right or left turn requires a signal. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R21 | anchor: A49
The described Sideroad warning identifies a road joining from the right and calls for watching entering vehicles. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R22 | anchor: A49
At a roundabout warning, reduce speed and yield to vehicles approaching from the left that are already circulating. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R23 | anchor: A49
A merging-traffic warning from the right calls for adjusting speed and lane position to permit a safe merge. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R24 | anchor: A49
A Railroad Crossing warning calls for yielding and readiness to stop for an approaching train. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R25 | anchor: A49
A No Train Horn sign below a railroad warning identifies an established quiet zone. [A49]
Source: [A49 -> pdf-0049]

FACT_ID: sec08-R26 | anchor: A50
Green-and-white guide signs provide directions and distances. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R27 | anchor: A50
Interchange guide diagrams direct drivers toward entrances and exits. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R28 | anchor: A50
The handbook requires a slow-moving-vehicle emblem on public roads for slow vehicles such as farm equipment travelling at twenty-five miles per hour or less. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R29 | anchor: A50
Blue-and-white service signs point to facilities such as hospitals, fuel, food and lodging. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R30 | anchor: A50
A yellow no-passing pennant may stand on the road's left side at the beginning of a no-passing zone. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R31 | anchor: A50
Nebraska highway reference posts appear at one-mile intervals and help identify a location when assistance is needed. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R32 | anchor: A50
Accessible parking spaces are reserved for people with the corresponding parking privileges. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R33 | anchor: A50
Route markers may appear alone or with directional arrows mounted underneath. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R34 | anchor: A50
Dynamic message signs change their messages to reflect conditions, route traffic or give construction and incident information. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R35 | anchor: A50
Most dynamic message signs are fixed along freeways, while portable signs can serve work sites, special events or major incidents. [A50]
Source: [A50 -> pdf-0050]

FACT_ID: sec08-R36 | anchor: A51
Black lettering on orange warning signs identifies a highway work zone. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R37 | anchor: A51
Work-zone signs can warn before the work area and also give directions within it. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R38 | anchor: A51
Stay alert when black-on-orange warnings indicate that a work zone is approaching. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R39 | anchor: A51
Advance work-zone warnings may call for changing lanes or reducing speed. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R40 | anchor: A51
Respond to advance work-zone directions early rather than waiting until the last moment and impeding traffic. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R41 | anchor: A51
Large flashing or sequential arrow panels can direct drivers to particular lanes and warn that roadway ahead is closed. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R42 | anchor: A51
Most work-zone warning signs have a diamond shape and warn of unusual conditions near the work. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R43 | anchor: A51
A Flagger warning calls for alertness and readiness to stop where a worker controls traffic. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R44 | anchor: A51
The handbook describes a flagger in a bright reflective orange vest using a STOP/SLOW paddle to control vehicles. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R45 | anchor: A51
If a flagger stops you, remain stopped until that flagger directs you to proceed. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]

FACT_ID: sec08-R46 | anchor: A51
Barricades, vertical panels, drums and cones commonly guide vehicles through a work zone. [A51]
Source: [A51 -> pdf-0051]
